author_note: independent reference authored without access to the tool code
reference: Synthetic incident-investigation corpus built around one conveyor hand-injury chain (organisational factor -> equipment state -> human action -> outcome, one failed barrier, one grounded action) and single-fault mutations of it, plus a multi-finding synthetic set, deletion/repair/loop/round-trip integrity cases, insufficient-data cases, exchange/file refusals and 10 randomized DAG investigations (seed 20260916). Expectations come from HSE HSG245 (cause levels, 'operator error ... sole cause ... rarely acceptable', missing/inadequate risk control measures, action plan timescale and responsible person), spec 04 rules and acceptance criteria, spec 00 section 0.5, and graph first principles computed by ref.py (counts, DFS cycle detection, reverse reachability, reference repair, datetime ordering). Rule IDs are the README's vocabulary; their expectations are derived from the cited basis, not from the tool.
reference_citations: HSE, HSG245 Investigating accidents and incidents: a workbook for employers, unions, safety representatives and safety professionals, 2004, ISBN 978 0 7176 2827 8, https://www.hse.gov.uk/pubns/hsg245.pdf (PDF pages 4-5 definitions; p.9; p.10; p.11; p.14; p.25)
tools.petrov.re spec 04 Incident Causal Tree (MVP scope, model rules, outputs, acceptance criteria) and spec 00-common section 0.5
Graph and time first principles: bench/incidenttree/ref.py (stdlib; DFS, reverse BFS, datetime)
tolerance: All checks exact: outcomes are categorical (finding present/absent, refused, state) or integer counts/id lists from discrete graph operations, where any deviation is a logic difference, not numerical error. Time comparisons are on whole minutes; equality is read as not 'after' (flagged disputable).
